chmmc-2021-proof-01.prompt: Find all ordered triples $(a,b,c)$ of real numbers such that $$(a-b)(b-c)+(b-c)(c-a)+(c-a)(a-b)=0.$$

chmmc-2021-proof-02.prompt: For any positive integer $n$, let $p(n)$ be the product of its digits in base-$10$ representation. Find the maximum possible value of $\frac{p(n)}n$ over all integers $n\ge10$.

chmmc-2021-proof-03a.prompt:
A polynomial $F(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ with real coefficients is called *$n$-alternating* if for all $1\le i<j\le n$, swapping $x_i$ and $x_j$ flips the sign of $F$, i.e. $F(\dots,x_i,\dots,x_j,\dots)=-F(\dots,x_j,\dots,x_i,\dots)$. For example, $x_1^2x_2-x_2^2x_1$ is $2$-alternating, whereas $x_1x_2x_3+2x_2x_3$ is not $3$-alternating.

Compute a $3$-alternating polynomial of degree $3$.

chmmc-2021-proof-03b.prompt:
A polynomial $F(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ ($n>1$) with real coefficients is called *$n$-alternating* if for all $1\le i<j\le n$, swapping $x_i$ and $x_j$ flips the sign of $F$. (Two polynomials are equal iff all their monomials have the same coefficients.)

Prove that the degree of any nonzero $n$-alternating polynomial is at least $\binom n2$.
chmmc-2021-proof-03b.answer: Every monomial of $F$ has distinct exponents $k_1,\dots,k_n$, so its degree is at least $0+1+\dots+(n-1)=\binom n2$.

chmmc-2021-proof-04.prompt: Show that for any three positive integers $a,m,n$ such that $m$ divides $n$, there exists an integer $k$ such that $\gcd(a,m)=\gcd(a+km,n)$.
chmmc-2021-proof-04.answer: Reduce to $\gcd(a,m)=1$ and take $k$ = product of the primes dividing $n$ but neither $a$ nor $m$.

chmmc-2021-proof-05.prompt: Find all functions $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that $$f\big(f(x)+f(y)^2\big)=f(x)^2+y^2f(y)^3.$$

chmmc-2021-proof-06.answer: $L$ is the $A$-Humpty point; the midpoint $X$ of $AL$ lies on the nine-point circle, and both $M_1,M_2$ lie on line $DX$.
